LESSON: SCRIPTURAL STORIES AND FAMILY VALUES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Scriptures (Dharam Granths)
Topic 3.1: Scriptural Stories and Family Values

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Scriptural Stories and Family Values. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do Scriptures contribute to instilling moral values?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values
2. demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths
3. appreciate the role of Scriptures for character moulding

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SCRIPTURAL STORIES AND FAMILY VALUES
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Scriptural Stories and Family Values helps you succeed in HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: SCRIPTURAL STORIES AND FAMILY VALUES
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Scriptural Stories and Family Values” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Scriptural Stories and Family Values.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of Scriptures for character moulding

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of Scriptures for character moulding. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of Scriptures for character moulding.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of Scriptures for character moulding. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Scriptural Stories and Family Values is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Scriptural Stories and Family Values” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Scriptural Stories and Family Values. (skill: demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate the role of Scriptures for character moulding)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Scriptural Stories and Family Values to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of Scriptures for character moulding.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Scriptural Stories and Family Values from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Scriptural Stories and Family Values: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Scriptural Stories and Family Values?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do Scriptures contribute to instilling moral values?
2. How can we apply moral values in different situations in the family?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Scriptural Stories and Family Values means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the teachings of Scriptures at family level for development of moral values.
5. Be able to: demonstrate the teachings that promote moral values in families as per selected Scriptures from the four faiths.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
